title: The ISN Registry
subtitle: Guantánamo & the Manufacture of Lawlessness
abstract: GSS Anarchive · Collection 05. On arrival at Guantánamo Bay a man stopped being a name and became an Internment Serial Number. This counter-archive adopts that unit and turns it against itself: 780 marks, one per person ever held, arranged as a wall; ten registry files indexed by ISN; a twenty-four year chronology; a five-part legal-architecture diagram (the Lease, the Category, the Number, the Commission, the Ban on Exit). Names are put back beside numbers. Design conceit: the number is the archival unit — adopted in order to be broken. Refuses trophy imagery and torture-derived statements. Fifteen men remain inside as the page is served.
